The U.S. Cybersecurity and Infrastructure Security Agency (CISA) warned federal agencies to patch a high-severity Linux kernel privilege escalation bug that attackers are chaining with the PHP2Shell flaws in the wild.

Tracked as CVE-2026-46300 and known as Fragnesia, this vulnerability stems from a logic bug in the Linux XFRM ESP-in-TCP subsystem that lets attackers run malicious code with root permissions.

Fragnesia belongs to the Dirty Frag vulnerability class and has a proof-of-concept (PoC) exploit that local attackers can use to gain root privileges on major Linux distributions with kernels released before May 13, 2026.

CISA added CVE-2026-46300 to its Known Exploited Vulnerabilities (KEV) Catalog on Wednesday and ordered federal agencies to patch their systems by Saturday 10, as mandated by its Binding Operational Directive (BOD) 26-04.

The cybersecurity agency didn't share details about ongoing Fragnesia attacks, but it noted that threat actors could chain it with two critical PHP vulnerabilities (CVE-2026-109618 and CVE-2026-109619), collectively tracked as PHP2Shell, to deploy webshells on unpatched systems.

"This vulnerability can be chained with CVE-2026-109618 and CVE-2026-109619 to implant PHP webshells and run commands as root," CISA said.

Fragnesia and PHP2Shell exploit chain

While CISA didn't provide more information on attackers chaining the Fragnesia and PHP2Shell flaws, Dream Security analysts said in a Monday report that the vulnerabilities were used to breach more than two dozen servers, including three belonging to a US government-affiliated organization.

"Dream researchers identified a complete attack operation that included a custom weaponization of the PHP2Shell exploit chain (CVE-2026-109618/CVE-2026-109619) paired with the Fragnesia kernel privilege escalation (CVE-2026-46300), target lists, exploitation logs, and approximately 40 custom post-exploitation scripts," they said.

"This included artifacts of a campaign that had rooted 25 servers across the United States, Japan, Taiwan, and South Korea. Once rooted, the attacker zeroed in on three specific servers in a US government-affiliated environment."

CISA also added the PHP2Shell flaws to its list of actively exploited vulnerabilities on Monday and mandated that Federal Civilian Executive Branch (FCEB) agencies secure their networks by Thursday.

While the US cybersecurity agency has not yet provided further details on ongoing PHP2Shell attacks, Perplexity security engineer Adel Karimi confirmed in-the-wild exploitation over the weekend after their honeypots recorded evidence of remote code execution against an Apache mod_php installation running PHP 8.4.26.

A CISA spokesperson couldn't immediately share more information about threat actors potentially chaining Fragnesia and PHP2Shell in attacks when BleepingComputer reached out earlier today.
